claims.text: In PostgreSQL the default isolation level is Read Committed; under it, each query (SELECT) sees only data committed before the query began, so a query starting after a transaction commits sees that transaction's changes.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, 13.2 Transaction Isolation and 13.2.1 Read Committed Isolation Level

claims.text: At stage-3 each service has its own database: the order lives in donhang (DonHang.Api), refund rows in donhang_payments (DonHang.Payments).

Refund saga order: Api sets refunding + order.refund-requested outbox row; Payments saves a pending refund row, a background job asks the gateway and saves refunded + payment.refunded; Api then sets cancelled. Between Payments' commit and Api's handling, refund is refunded while order is refunding.
While DonHang.Payments is stopped, order.refund-requested stays in the RabbitMQ queue payments.refund-requests (1 message waiting) and is delivered once Payments starts again; the count drops to 0.
Payments' background job retries the gateway after 1, 2, 4, 8 minutes, at most 1 hour apart, for up to 24 hours from requested_at (YC-10); stated in sections 4 and 6.

The outbox keeps a committed step's message from being lost; the queue keeps it until Payments handles it or, past the delivery limit (x-delivery-limit 5), dead-letters it to payments.refund-requests.dead.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Payments/RabbitMqTopology.cs; DonHang.Messaging/RabbitMqPublisher.cs; RabbitMQ docs, Quorum Queues (poison message handling)

claims.text: payments-down.sh stops payments, requests a refund of order 10, waits 5 s, prints status, queue count, refund rows; starts payments, waits for cancelled, prints again. order_10 prints the GET status; waiting_in_queue polls rabbitmqctl up to 15 s for the given count, prints the count read.
payments-down.sh output: 202; 5 s later refunding, 1 message waiting in payments.refund-requests, 0 refund rows; after Payments is back cancelled, 0 waiting, refund row refunded.

OrdersController.Refund does not call Payments: it checks the customer, calls orderService.RequestRefundAsync (refunding + outbox row in one transaction) and returns Accepted(ToDto(order)), i.e. 202 with the order's current status refunding.
ControllerBase.Accepted(object value) produces a 202 Accepted response with the value as body.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core API reference: ControllerBase.Accepted, AcceptedResult

claims.text: YC-4: after sending the request, the customer sees the order as being refunded and cannot send a second request. YC-7: the refund request is accepted and answered within 2 seconds, even when the gateway does not answer or errors.
A message moved to a dead-letter queue is not handled again until a person acts, so the services stay apart until then.
claims.source_hint: backend.l3.dead-letter-queue (stage-3 messaging module); examples/don-hang @ stage-3: STAGE.md:22-24 (dead-letter queue per service)

claims.text: Opinion: when the slow or stopped part is in another service, the endpoint should report the state it is sure of (refunding) instead of failing or waiting; failing would not remove the disagreement, which exists whenever a message is in flight.
